primary_claim: Activation plateaus in GPT-2 Large emerge and sharpen gradually across layers, are produced specifically by MLP blocks rather than attention blocks, persist without LayerNorm, and correspond to areas of high MLP input-output Jacobian sensitivity at their boundaries.

effect.metric: relative (L2) distance of model outputs across activation-space interpolation, and component-freezing effect on plateau formation
effect.value: freezing MLP block outputs completely eliminates plateaus; freezing attention block outputs has relatively small effect

contradicts_or_qualifies: Extends a prior interim research report on activation plateaus and sensitive directions by providing a general mechanistic explanation of where and how plateaus emerge
limitations_stated: Does not definitively rule out any LayerNorm involvement in producing plateaus, only that its role (if any) can be taken on by other MLP components
The LayerNorm-free model used was fine-tuned from a model that originally had LayerNorm, so a model trained from scratch without it might learn different mechanisms
Taking the L2 norm of the whole Jacobian is a simple aggregate sensitivity measure; other metrics (directional Jacobian, pullback measures, volume measures) might be better
quote: activation plateaus emerge and sharpen gradually across model layers, with later layers having a slightly weaker—but similar—effect.
